accepted.text: (Whole question) Note: Please mark parts (b) and (c) together for any of the three ways.
(Whole question) Note: The B1 mark (part (c)) should be awarded in the same place on ePEN as in the Way 1 approach.

(Whole question) Aliter Way 2: $\ln y = -\ln(x-1)+\ln(2x-3)^2+c$ M1 Using the power law for logarithms; $\ln y=\ln\left(\frac{(2x-3)^2}{x-1}\right)+c$ M1 Using the product and/or quotient laws for logarithms to obtain a single RHS logarithmic term with/without constant c. $\ln y=\ln\left(\frac{A(2x-3)^2}{x-1}\right)$ where $c=\ln A$ or $e^{\ln y}=e^{\ln\left(\frac{(2x-3)^2}{x-1}\right)+c}=e^{\ln\left(\frac{(2x-3)^2}{x-1}\right)}e^c$; $y=\frac{A(2x-3)^2}{(x-1)}$; $y=10, x=2$ gives $A=10$ ($A=10$ for B1, award above); $y=\frac{10(2x-3)^2}{(x-1)}$ or aef & isw A1 aef

(Whole question) Aliter Way 3: $\therefore \ln y=-\ln(x-1)+2\ln(x-\frac{3}{2})+\ln 40$; $\ln y=-\ln(x-1)+\ln(x-\frac{3}{2})^2+\ln 10$ M1 Using the power law for logarithms; $\ln y=\ln\left(\frac{(x-\frac{3}{2})^2}{(x-1)}\right)+\ln 40$ or $\ln y=\ln\left(\frac{40(x-\frac{3}{2})^2}{(x-1)}\right)$ M1 Using the product and/or quotient laws for logarithms to obtain a single RHS logarithmic term with/without constant c. $y=\frac{40(x-\frac{3}{2})^2}{(x-1)}$ or aef. isw A1 aef
